- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing sharp drops.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise after 2 consecutive days of high sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price > 75% of 30d moving avg, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overbought trap.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if last 5 days show strong downward sentiment, model often fails to anticipate drop — add 2–5% downward bias in final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 in 2 days), model often misjudges direction — adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal within 3–5 days.
